headline: High: shared filesystem and write access make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default between Claude Code and Flowise.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read/write repo files and uses MCP; Flowise reads/writes server filesystem and uploaded files. That creates a shared-file bridge where Flowise outputs or uploaded content can be treated as trusted input by Claude Code, even without clipboard or direct chat bridging. The pathway is plausible in default deployments, though not inherently guaranteed.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled text into a file that Claude Code later reads
IF Claude Code is configured to act on repository or workspace files as instructions
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files into Claude Code workflows
Add a manual review step before Claude Code processes Flowise outputs
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files exchanged between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and have broad network egress, so sensitive repo contents or uploaded files can flow from one agent into the other’s outputs or backend calls. Claude Code handles git credentials and shell environment; Flowise handles model provider keys and tool credentials. The shared filesystem/workspace makes leakage plausible in default setups, though not necessarily automatic.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or uploaded-file store
IF either agent forwards file contents to external model providers or tools
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Remove secrets from shared directories before running either agent
Limit Flowise uploads to sanitized copies only
Rotate exposed credentials after any shared-run test
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state; Flowise can also write the filesystem and shares state via server datastore. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes can clobber files or corrupt git history. Because both agents have write paths by default, the conflict is immediate and can cause irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or server filesystem
IF Flowise flows write artifacts while Claude Code edits or commits the same paths
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Pause one agent while the other writes git state
Use branch-per-agent workflows
Take a quick backup before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based orchestrator that can consume tool outputs, and Claude Code can generate code, facts, or commands that Flowise may route into downstream actions. If Flowise treats Claude Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into browser actions, API calls, or other tool nodes. The interaction is plausible and dangerous in default flow designs.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Claude Code output as an upstream node input without validation
IF downstream Flowise nodes execute browser or API actions based on that output
mitigations: Insert a human approval node before any action-taking step
Require schema validation on Claude Code outputs
Limit Flowise to read-only or dry-run flows
Log and diff intermediate outputs before execution
requires-engineering: add verification gates between generation and action nodes

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and local files, while Flowise handles uploaded files, model-provider keys, and tool credentials. If regulated data is placed into Flowise flows or shared workspaces, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Claude Code’s local terminal workflow. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Flowise flows
IF retention or logging settings differ between the terminal workspace and Flowise server datastore
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared flows
Review Flowise retention and logging settings
Keep Claude Code worktrees free of regulated records
Document which data classes each agent may process
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems
